rows.sub_theme: Electric vehicles: fleet transition, life-cycle emissions, cost, policy and barriers
rows.settings: sectors: transport 6. departments: Nariño 1; Bogotá D.C. 1; national/unspecified 4
rows.technical: EV vs ICEV taxi 16.67 vs 122.38 kWh/100 km [R0193]; ~2,140 chargers by 2030 and ~9,850 by 2040 [R0168]; Scenario 2 (about 50% hybrids) cuts energy use 24.64% (2035) and 33.81% (2040) [R0130]
rows.economic: EV 52.13% cheaper after 20 years [R0193]; 0.03 vs 0.07 USD/km [R0193]; accumulated cost 51,498.69 vs 108,203.09 USD [R0193]; without incentives EV cost +12.94% [R0193]; full passenger-transport electrification by 2050 cuts costs 40% [R1813]; 600,000 EVs in 2030 cut 3.5% [R1813]; ~1,070 direct jobs by 2030 and 4,925 by 2040 [R0168]; 38 sources selected (23 rail, 15 inland waterway) [R0066]
rows.environmental: BEV GWP 27.79%, 18.25%, 13.02% lower than petrol, diesel, natural gas cars but 9.01% above diesel bus [R0421]; 27.40 vs 217.75 g CO2/km [R0193]; CO2 savings 32,100 t (2030) and 147,750 t (2040) [R0168]; El Niño raises emissions up to 38%, La Niña lowers them 14% [R1813]
rows.pattern: Simulation and life-cycle studies agree that battery-electric options cut emissions and operating cost (27.40 vs 217.75 g CO2/km and EV 52.13% cheaper after 20 years in R0193; BEV GWP lower than petrol, diesel and natural gas cars but 9.01% above diesel bus in R0421; full passenger-transport electrification by 2050 cuts costs 40% in R1813), but the gain depends on context (El Niño raises emissions up to 38% in R1813; without incentives EV cost +12.94% in R0193). R0168 adds infrastructure and jobs figures (~2,140 chargers by 2030), R0130 a hybrid-fleet scenario, and R0066 is a review of rail and inland-waterway sources (38 sources selected).

rows.sub_theme: Buildings: envelope materials, passive comfort, energy performance, HVAC selection and demand management
rows.settings: sectors: buildings-residential 3; buildings-commercial-institutional 1. departments: Bogotá D.C. 1; Cundinamarca 1; Magdalena 1; Atlántico 1; Sucre 1
rows.technical: indoor temperature reduction 1.5% to 16% house by house, average 7.19% [R0121]; EnPI 12.67 (split) vs 8.03 kWh/m2-month (VRF, -36.6%) [R0271]; EMS+PV saves 10% (Design 1) and 19.11% (Design 2) [R0029]; total-consumption MSE 0.00093, R2 0.6562 [R0428]
rows.economic: LCC savings 20% (VRF), 16% (VAV), 13% (chiller) [R0271]; with 100% PV subsidy payback is 8 (D1) and 6 years (D2) [R0029]
rows.environmental: CO2 emissions fall about 85-86% vs grid [R0029]
rows.pattern: The four building studies use different outcome metrics (average indoor temperature reduction 7.19% in R0121; EnPI 12.67 (split) vs 8.03 kWh/m2-month (VRF, -36.6%) and LCC savings of 20% (VRF), 16% (VAV) and 13% (chiller) in R0271; EMS+PV savings of 10% and 19.11% with payback of 8 and 6 years under a 100% PV subsidy in R0029; a forecasting model with MSE 0.00093 and R2 0.6562 in R0428), so results are not directly comparable.

rows.sub_theme: Industrial energy efficiency, demand management, rebound and national-level efficiency policy
rows.settings: sectors: industry 2; buildings-residential 1; non-interconnected-zones 1; power-generation-SIN 1; multi-sector 1. departments: Antioquia 1; Atlántico 1; Bogotá D.C. 1; Bolívar 1; Boyacá 1; Caldas 1; Cundinamarca 1; Córdoba 1; Huila 1; Magdalena 1; Meta 1; Risaralda 1; Santander 1; Tolima 1; Valle del Cauca 1; Guaviare 1; national/unspecified 4
rows.technical: national long-term direct rebound effect 83.4% [R0038]; peak-hour reduction 52.5 kWh/day [R0050]; daily consumption falls from 941.5 to 738.3 kWh/day [R0050]; 95.3% efficiency in hydro [R0192]
rows.environmental: 213,039 kgCO2/year [R0235]; 4.12 in 2022 kg CO2-eq/m2, forecast 4.46 kg CO2-eq/m2 by 2030 [R0408]; CO2 reduction about 10 TonEq/year [R0050]; carbon intensity 61.8 kgCO2eq/USD [R0192]
rows.pattern: The evidence is heterogeneous: a national long-term direct rebound effect of 83.4% (R0038); consumption falling from 941.5 to 738.3 kWh/day with billing savings of USD 119.5/day (R0050); 95.3% efficiency in hydro and carbon intensity 61.8 kgCO2eq/USD (R0192); and emissions of 213,039 kgCO2/year (R0235) or 4.12 in 2022 kg CO2-eq/m2 (R0408). Metrics and units differ across studies, so no pooled comparison is possible.
